An invoice is arithmetic and layout: line items, a VAT rate per line, a subtotal, a total, and a page that has to look like a document rather than a spreadsheet.

`invoice` takes the line items as front matter and does the rest.
The totals table is computed from the quantities, unit prices, and VAT rates, and the page is laid out through Typst.

[See one rendered by this site](preview.pdf).

## Starting an invoice

```bash
quarto use template {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

## Adding it to a document you already have

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

## Quick start

```yaml
format:
  invoice-typst:
    sender:
      name: "Example Consulting Ltd"
    recipient:
      name: "Director Doe & Co"
    invoice:
      number: "INV-2026-001"
      issued: 2026-05-01
      due: 2026-05-31
      currency: GBP
      items:
        - description: Strategy workshop
          quantity: 2
          unit-price: 1500
          vat: 20
```

```bash
quarto render invoice.qmd --to invoice-typst
```

`sender`, `recipient`, and `invoice` are required; the rest is filled in when it is given.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for a branded invoice and a hand-written table.

## Where it works

PDF, through Typst.

Typst ships with Quarto, so nothing else has to be installed.
